task.title: Put the shell's wordmark and the board's header in the window's title row
task.description:
Dylan, 2026-10-08, with Slack as the model: the title strip over the board carries only the project name and adds nothing, so remove it. Move the board's own header up to the top edge so its REPOSITORY: <name> eyebrow lines up with the sidebar's WORKBENCH wordmark, and move the wordmark and the sidebar collapse button up into the same row as the window controls (the traffic lights on macOS, the overlay controls on Windows). Everything in that row is part of the drag target; only the collapse button, and the board header's own buttons, links and inputs, keep working as controls and take precedence over the drag.

Consequences, settled with Dylan: the board view is laid out from y=0 again and the board page's header becomes the window's drag region when the page runs inside Workbench (the shell's preload already marks the document in-workbench); the shell keeps the sidebar head as its own drag area; the version line stays under the wordmark, so the sidebar head is a little taller than the board's eyebrow row. On macOS pin the traffic-light position explicitly so the row is a known height and the wordmark starts to their right; on Windows the board header must keep its right-hand controls clear of the window-controls overlay (the overlay's env(titlebar-area-*) values, with the preload telling the page the platform), and the overlay height follows the new row. Linux keeps native decorations and no inset. The sidebar divider from PR #163 still stops at the board header's bottom edge. Verify with screenshots in both themes: wordmark and eyebrow on one baseline, the chevron level with the traffic lights, the board starting at the top edge, and a computed-style read that the header is a drag region with its controls opted out.
